newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK, U.S. probe senior U.S. immigration official.
newsitem.headline: HK, U.S. probe senior U.S. immigration official.

text.p: Hong Kong's anti-graft body and the U.S. Justice Department are investigating a senior U.S. immigration official in the territory and his wife for suspected corruption and abuse of authority, an official said on Sunday.

A U.S. consulate spokesman, Patrick Corcoran, told Reuters the joint probe was of James DeBates, acting chief of the U.S. Immigration and Naturalization Service office in Hong Kong, and his wife Heddy.
He said they were being investigated by the territory's Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC) and the Office of the Inspector General of the U.S. Justice Department.

Earlier, the ICAC said in a statement that it and the U.S. authority were jointly investigating allegations of corruption and abuse of authority by a Hong Kong-based U.S. Immigration and Naturalization Service official and his wife.
The ICAC statement did not name the people involved.
"The enquiries, which are still continuing, are conducted with the full knowledge and co-operation of the U.S. Consulate General in Hong Kong," it said, without giving further details.

The South China Morning Post newspaper said on Sunday that a U.S. Immigration and Naturalization Service official had been suspended as part of an international probe into the suspected smuggling of illegal immigrants from China to the United States.
The ICAC was not immediately available to comment.
Heddy DeBates said the couple had no objection to being investigated.
"Yes, that's okay. They can investigate. No problem... I really don't know what to tell you because you know (if) they want to investigate they can investigate," she said by telephone.
Both Corcoran and Heddy DeBates said the U.S. immigration official was on administrative leave.
DeBates' wife said her husband was in the United States. She said the ICAC had detained her, but declined to comment further.
Last July, another U.S. immigration officer, Jerry Stuchiner, was arrested by the ICAC in conjuction with U.S. Justice Department officials investigating an immigrant smuggling ring.
He later received a 40-month jail sentence for possessing forged passports of Honduras, where he had worked for the U.S. Immigration Service.
The smuggling of illegal immigrants from Asia, including China, into the United States had long been a concern for Washington. Some of the smuggling networks have involved Hong Kong and its people.
